frames.title: Cut to serve pulse, clarity, and revelation
frames.summary: Rhythm is not just speed; it is the felt timing of information, emotion, and momentum.
principles: Cut when the audience needs a new idea, emphasis, or energy shift.
Hold longer when performance or tension is still evolving inside the shot.
Use variation in shot duration to create musical contrast.
Protect spatial and emotional continuity unless disorientation is intentional.
patterns: Let reaction timing determine many of the strongest cuts.
Use montage compression when accumulation matters more than coverage detail.
antiPatterns: Do not equate faster cutting with stronger intensity.
Do not flatten every scene into the same editorial tempo.

frames.title: Use sound to shape world, tension, and subjectivity
frames.summary: Sound design can carry emotional perspective, hidden threat, and scale long before the image states it plainly.
principles: Decide what the audience should hear literally versus psychologically.
Build contrast between silence, ambience, and impact events.
Use sonic motifs to connect memory, threat, or character presence.
Layer detail according to story focus rather than maximum density.
patterns: Introduce offscreen sound before visual reveal to create anticipation.
Use perspective shifts in sound field to signal subjectivity.
antiPatterns: Do not fill every gap with undifferentiated texture.
Do not let music and effects fight for the same narrative job.

frames.title: Give actors playable direction
frames.summary: Strong direction translates abstract intention into action, stakes, and relationship behavior.
principles: Frame notes around verbs, objectives, and obstacles.
Protect the actor's inner logic even when adjusting tone or pace.
Give contradictions room when they make the moment human.
Align performance calibration with the camera's distance and scene purpose.
patterns: Offer one note that changes behavior before offering several that change result.
Use specific image or relationship prompts when emotional labels are too vague.
antiPatterns: Do not direct only by adjectives like 'more intense' or 'less flat'.
Do not chase line readings that erase truthful spontaneity.
